message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will build a Java project with Maven, and cache/restore any dependencies to improve the workflow execution time
# For more information see: https://help.github.com/actions/language-and-framework-guides/building-and-testing-java-with-maven

name: Java CI with Gradle

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Set up JDK 17
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: '17'
        distribution: 'adopt'
        #cache: maven
    - name: Cache Gradle dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.gradle/caches
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') }}
    - name: Build with Gradle
      run: |
        ./gradlew shadowJar --no-daemon
        mkdir staging/ && cp dev.skidfuscator.client.standalone/build/libs/client-standalone-all.jar staging
    - name: Upload a Build Artifact
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3.1.0
      with:
        name: Skidfuscator.jar
        path: staging/client-standalone-all.jar",
  "rationale": "The workflow builds a Gradle Java project but has no dependency cache step. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE, including a measured Gradle experiment (experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200) showing ~20.4% median elapsed-time reduction from caching ~/.gradle/caches keyed by gradle files, supports adding a cache step before the build. Prerequisites are met: repeated dependency fetching occurs and cache inputs (build.gradle/gradle-wrapper.properties) are available. The change is minimal and preserves the existing build, test, and artifact steps unchanged.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
